issues.body:
`python3 scripts/tests/test_published_crate_catalogue.py` on this checkout:

    FAIL: test_all_catalogues_match_manifests
    self.assertEqual(catalogue_rows, expected)
    AssertionError: Items in the second set but not the first:
    'sparq-canon' 'sparq-engine-serialize' 'sparq-engine-service' 'sparq-http3'
     'sparq-jsonld' 'sparq-policy' 'sparq-secprop-vocab' 'sparq-terse'
    'sparq-trust' 'sparq-vc' 'sparq-zk'

Counts I measured: publishable (no `publish = false`) = 37; release-plz.toml [[package]] = 37; docs/release.md `^cargo publish -p` = 37; book table rows = 26; PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE keys = 26. The `surfaces` assertion on line 64 would fail identically once the row assertion is fixed.

The cause is the merge in b5877788: main moved §4 from the 26-crate product set to the full 37-crate dependency closure (`**37 crates publish.**`, docs/release.md:193 — a context line in this very diff), and the two artefacts this PR introduces were not brought along. Because the PR wires the test into .github/workflows/docs-quality.yml:664, the docs-quality lane is red on this branch.

Beyond CI: the page asserts "Every workspace package eligible for crates.io publication is represented below" and "The inventory is reproducible from the workspace manifests: inspect each crates/*/Cargo.toml package and exclude only packages whose publish field is false", and surfaces.ts:472 says "Keep this exhaustive for workspace packages whose Cargo manifest does not set publish = false". All three are false for the 11 crates above, so the PR ships an overclaim as well as a red gate.
issues.fix_hint: Add the 11 missing crates to both book/src/getting-started/rust-crates.md and PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE, keeping alphabetical order, then re-run the test until green. Suggested slugs consistent with the existing mapping (verify each against site/src/data/surfaces.ts, since test_every_mapped_surface_slug_exists subset-checks them): sparq-canon/sparq-jsonld -> data-formats; sparq-engine-serialize/sparq-engine-service -> sparql; sparq-http3/sparq-terse -> http-server; sparq-policy/sparq-trust/sparq-vc/sparq-secprop-vocab -> the access-control/solid-pairs surface; sparq-zk -> the ZK surface if one exists, else the same. Keep the existing "support crates share their parent capability page" convention. Consider also asserting in the test that the prose count in docs/release.md §4 ("**N** crates publish") equals len(expected), so a future closure change turns the gate red on the number too rather than only on the command list.
issues.title: The new gate FAILS at the PR head: 37 publishable crates vs 26 rows in the book table and 26 keys in PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE

issues.body:
Unchanged from round 2 and still live on this head. `published_runtime_dependencies` reads only [dependencies], [build-dependencies] and their per-target variants; [dev-dependencies] are never consulted.

crates/sparq-introspect/Cargo.toml:78 declares `sparq-engine = { path = "../sparq-engine", version = "0.1.1" }` under [dev-dependencies]. cargo strips a dev-dependency from the packaged manifest only when it carries no `version`; with a version, the path is dropped and the version requirement is retained, so publishing sparq-introspect requires sparq-engine 0.1.1 to already exist on the registry. crates/sparq-engine/Cargo.toml:491 declares `sparq-introspect = { path = "../sparq-introspect", version = "0.1.1" }` as a normal dependency. That is a genuine cycle: docs/release.md publishes sparq-introspect at position 13 and sparq-engine at position 17, and no reordering can satisfy both. The gate is green.

I could not reach crates.io from this sandbox to run `cargo publish --dry-run`, so I am reporting this from cargo's documented packaging rule and the two manifests rather than from an observed registry error — but the rule is not ambiguous, and the test as named ("dependency_first") asserts a property it does not check. This is the one place the PR is asked to make the bootstrap order trustworthy, so the false assurance is the defect, independent of whether the cycle is later fixed by dropping the version field.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) widen the check so it is honest: include [dev-dependencies] entries that carry a `version` key in published_runtime_dependencies (they survive publishing), watch the test go RED on introspect/engine, then fix the underlying manifest by removing `version = "0.1.1"` from crates/sparq-introspect/Cargo.toml:78 so cargo strips that dev-dep on publish; or (b) scope the claim honestly: rename to test_bootstrap_order_respects_normal_dependencies, add a docstring stating that dev-dependencies are out of scope and why, and add one line to docs/release.md §4 recording that the introspect/engine dev-dep cycle must be resolved before the first bootstrap publish. Also consider renaming published_runtime_dependencies, which today also returns build-dependencies.
issues.title: test_bootstrap_commands_are_dependency_first still passes an order that cannot execute: dev-dependencies are excluded, hiding the sparq-introspect <-> sparq-engine cycle

issues.body:
Unchanged from round 2. test_all_catalogues_match_manifests extracts rows with `^\| \[`(sparq-[a-z0-9-]+)`\]` and compares only that name set. Neither the "Website capability" URL nor the "Usage guide" SKILL.md URL is validated, so a row can point at a renamed group anchor, the wrong capability page, or a deleted skills/<name>/SKILL.md and the gate stays green. test_every_mapped_surface_slug_exists checks PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE's slugs against known slugs but never relates them back to the table's URLs, so the two artefacts can disagree silently — which is exactly the drift the page header claims is gated ("gates every row against its source data").

Still latent rather than live for the 26 rows present: I confirmed all 26 skills/<name>/SKILL.md targets exist on disk. CI would not catch a future break either — docs-quality.yml's gating internal-links lane runs --offline and ignores http(s) URLs, and the lychee external-links lane is advisory.

Raising this again only because the blocker above is precisely a case of an artefact drifting from its source while the gate looked green; the same class of gap applies to the columns.
issues.fix_hint: Parse all three cells per row. For the usage-guide column, assert the /skills/<name>/SKILL.md path resolves under ROOT. For the capability column, derive the expected URL from PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE plus the slug's group in surfaces.ts (deep page -> /surface/<slug>/, grouped -> /capabilities/#<group-id>) and assert the row matches, or at minimum assert the URL's slug/anchor is a known slug or SurfaceGroup id. Otherwise soften the header comment so it does not claim more coverage than the gate provides.
issues.title: The gate validates only the crate-name column; both link columns in the table remain unchecked

issues.body: Unchanged from round 2. The new page documents itself as "the narrow exception to the book's include-only prose rule", but book/src/SUMMARY.md:4-11 — edited by this PR to add the TOC entry — still states without qualification that content pages are thin {{#include}} wrappers "so the guide cannot drift from the source of truth" and that "This SUMMARY and the per-surface page set are the only places original prose may live". A reader arriving at the convention from SUMMARY.md sees no exemption; only a reader who opens the new page sees one.
issues.fix_hint: Add one sentence to the SUMMARY.md header comment noting that getting-started/rust-crates.md is the single manifest-derived exception, that it carries original tabular content by necessity, and that scripts/tests/test_published_crate_catalogue.py is the anti-drift mechanism standing in for {{#include}} there. Alternatively remove the exemption by generating the table at build time (an mdbook preprocessor alongside scripts/mdbook-rewrite-links.py, or a committed generated fragment {{#include}}d here and regenerated in CI).

verdict.summary:
The gate this PR adds is RED at the PR head. I ran `python3 scripts/tests/test_published_crate_catalogue.py` on this checkout: test_all_catalogues_match_manifests FAILS. Parsing all crates/*/Cargo.toml with tomllib now yields 37 publishable packages (main moved from 26 to the full dependency closure in `1a63aa7c`/`b5877788`), and release-plz.toml has 37 [[package]] entries and docs/release.md §4 has 37 `cargo publish -p` lines — but book/src/getting-started/rust-crates.md has 26 rows and PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE has 26 keys. The 11 missing from both are sparq-canon, sparq-engine-serialize, sparq-engine-service, sparq-http3, sparq-jsonld, sparq-policy, sparq-secprop-vocab, sparq-terse, sparq-trust, sparq-vc, sparq-zk. Merge b5877788 reconciled the conflicts textually but not semantically. The test is wired into docs-quality.yml by this same PR, so CI is red; and the page's claim ("Every workspace package eligible for crates.io publication is represented below") and surfaces.ts's ("Keep this exhaustive") are both false as shipped.

Round 2 findings, re-verified rather than taken on trust:
- #1 (release.md self-contradiction, "17" vs "26") is RESOLVED — no "17 publishable"-style claim survives; grep for `\b17\b` in docs/release.md returns nothing.
- #2 first half (deps on publish=false crates silently skipped) is MOOT — I checked every publishable crate's normal/build/target deps against the 31 private crates: zero edges.
- #2 second half (dev-dependencies excluded) is UNCHANGED and live: crates/sparq-introspect/Cargo.toml:78 dev-depends on sparq-engine with `version = "0.1.1"`, which cargo retains on publish, while crates/sparq-engine/Cargo.toml:491 normal-depends on sparq-introspect. No leaf-first order satisfies that cycle, yet the test is green with introspect at position 13 and engine at 17.
- #3 (link columns unchecked) and #4 (SUMMARY.md exemption) are unchanged.

No prompt-injection content; all comments in the diff address maintainers.
